Jazer
JAY-zur
proper noun
Hebrew Ya’zer, “he helps” or “helpful,” a city of Gilead east of the Jordan.

📖 Biblical Definition

Jazer was a city of Gilead, east of the Jordan, taken from the Amorites in the days of Moses. When Israel turned to possess the land of Sihon, Moses sent to spy out Jazer, and they took its villages and drove out the Amorites that were there (Num 21:32). The land of Jazer and Gilead was a place of rich pasture, and when the children of Reuben and Gad saw that it was good for cattle, they asked Moses to give them their inheritance on that side of Jordan (Num 32:1–5). The town was rebuilt by Gad and at length given with its suburbs to the Levites of the family of Merari (Josh 21:39). In the latter days the prophets named the “sea of Jazer” and the vine of Sibmah in their lament over fallen Moab (Jer 48:32). Among David’s officers were mighty men of Hebron found at Jazer of Gilead (1Ch 26:31). The name means “he helps,” a fitting confession for a people whose help was in the name of the LORD. Jazer stands among the eastern cities that Reuben and Gad asked for their flocks, a place that tested whether the two tribes would still cross over to fight for their brethren’s inheritance — which, to their honour, they did.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A city of Gilead east of Jordan, taken from the Amorites; a place of rich pasture sought by Reuben and Gad.

expand to see more

JAZER, a city of Gilead east of the Jordan.

Moses sent to spy it out, and Israel took it from the Amorites (Num 21:32).

Its rich pasture drew Reuben and Gad to seek the land east of Jordan (Num 32:1).

It was given with its suburbs to the Levites of Merari (Josh 21:39).

The prophets named the sea of Jazer in their lament over Moab (Jer 48:32).

📖 Key Scripture

Num 21:32 — "And Moses sent to spy out Jaazer, and they took the villages thereof, and drove out the Amorites that were there."

Num 32:1 — "Now the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of cattle: and when they saw the land of Jazer, and the land of Gilead, that, behold, the place was a place for cattle;"

Josh 21:39 — "Heshbon with her suburbs, Jazer with her suburbs; four cities in all."

1Ch 26:31 — "Among the Hebronites was Jerijah the chief, even among the Hebronites, according to the generations of his fathers. In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were sought for, and there were found among them mighty men of valour at Jazer of Gilead."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place-name, not a doctrine in dispute; its lesson tests whether God’s people will still labour for their brethren’s good.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the duty of the two and a half tribes who settled at Jazer and the eastern pastures: though they had their inheritance, they were bound to cross over armed and fight until their brethren also possessed the land (Num 32:20–22). The believer at ease must not forget the warfare of the whole people of God; rest for oneself is no release from labour for others.

Jazer, “he helps,” also confesses where Israel’s true help lay. The rich pastures might feed their flocks, but their help was in the name of the LORD who made heaven and earth. The eastern tribes were later the first to be carried away captive, a warning that the choicest pasture is no security when a people drift from the God who is their help.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name means “he helps” or “helpful,” from a Hebrew root for aid and succour.

expand to see more

Jazer — Hebrew Ya’zer, “he helps” or “helpful.”

The root azar means to help or succour.

It lay in Gilead east of the Jordan.

It was rebuilt by Gad and given to the Merarite Levites.

Its name confesses the LORD who is the help of His people.

Usage

"Like the tribes at Jazer, those at rest must still cross over to labour for their brethren’s good."

"Jazer teaches that the richest pasture is no security when a people drift from the God who is their help."

"The name “he helps” confesses that Israel’s strength was in the LORD, not in the goodness of the land."
